evidence_quotes.quote: In response to these challenges, rainwater has been explored as an appropriate solution for the provision of clean water to rural communities in the Amazon basin.

To identify stakeholders, the respondents were asked to 1) mention all stakeholders and issues that may influence or are affected by the implementation of water infrastructure - rainwater systems. 2) Quantify the influence of each stakeholder exerts on water infrastructure planning

In the current implementation lead by UFPA, note the brokerage from SEASTER, AMAE, and CARITAS, evidenced by their intermediation in the network “connecting” funding agencies and recipient communities.

The methodological design followed a two-stage explorative research process where stakeholders were identified and classified based on an iterative process that drew on a combination of methods (e.g. 6 expert opinions - semi-structured interviews in English and Portuguese; ethnographic observations in 16 municipalities involving 40 user families)

The following figure (figure 1) reflects the results of the use of SNA for the mapping of issues and stakeholders related with the adoption of rainwater systems in Belem; where the values of centrality (degree) for UFPA, Residents, CARITAS, AMAE highlight the relevance of these stakeholders in the implementation of RTRWH.
Social learning process hindered; uncovered expectations in terms of number of units implemented; failure / abandonment of several installed units;

criterion_notes.c1: Yes. The paper examines the implementation of rooftop rainwater harvesting (RTRWH) water supply systems intended to provide clean drinking water to riverside island communities and households in Belém, Pará, Brazil, where public water supply is largely absent or non-potable.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording: Yes — the study examines governance in the implementation of community rainwater systems, focusing on stakeholder network centrality, institutional overlap, interagency brokerage for federal project funding, and community collective-action challenges in maintaining shared systems. Narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: No — the paper analyzes multi-stakeholder project delivery and technology-niche implementation ('Strategic Niche Management' and stakeholder influence on 'water infrastructure planning') for subsidized off-grid rainwater harvesting installations rather than a rule-type legal, regulatory, or administrative mechanism directly governing service access (such as eligibility screening, household administrative burden, documentation or tenure requirements, tariff or cost-recovery rules, frontline discretion or accommodation in granting service access, enforcement, or utility ownership/regulatory rules governing access). Although the authors invoke 'street-level bureaucracies' and 'regulatory capture,' they apply those terms to regional agencies, NGOs, and a university competing as intermediaries for federal project budgets rather than administrative rules governing household access.
criterion_notes.c3: Yes. The paper reports primary empirical research conducted in 2016 using a two-stage exploratory design combining 6 semi-structured expert interviews and ethnographic observations across 16 municipalities involving 40 user families, analyzed with Social Network Analysis (UCINET degree and betweenness centrality) and qualitative framework analysis (Strategic Niche Management and Safe-and-SuRe).
criterion_notes.c4: Unclear. The primary empirical outputs are stakeholder and issue network centrality rankings in RTRWH infrastructure planning (with Figures 1–3 missing as '[INSERT FIGURE ... HERE]' placeholders in this accepted-manuscript PDF) and qualitative accounts of project-delivery tensions (funding competition, education/maintenance gaps, interagency relationships, intra-community conflict, and lack of post-delivery monitoring). System non-use or abandonment ('failure / abandonment of several installed units') is mentioned only briefly in one interview quote and the Safe-and-SuRe summary table rather than systematically assessed as a household or community water-access outcome.
criterion_notes.c5: Unclear. While the exploratory case-study/SNA design and data sources (6 experts, 16 municipalities, 40 user families; 14 Belém stakeholder nodes) are stated, Figures 1–3 reporting the quantitative SNA results are omitted as placeholders in the accepted manuscript, and the study does not operationalize a rule-type governance exposure linked to a household or community service-access outcome.
criterion_notes.c6: Yes. The full text is written in English, an eligible review language.

study_design: Exploratory qualitative case study and Social Network Analysis (SNA) based on semi-structured expert interviews and ethnographic observations
population_and_sample: 6 regional experts (semi-structured interviews) and ethnographic observations in 16 municipalities involving 40 user families; SNA network of 14 stakeholder groups and 5 implementation issues in Belém, Pará, Brazil
exposure: Stakeholder network structure (degree and betweenness centrality), interagency funding brokerage, and technology-niche governance in the project implementation of rooftop rainwater harvesting (RTRWH) systems
outcome: Stakeholder and issue centrality in water infrastructure planning/implementation (SNA figures omitted as placeholders in the accepted manuscript) and qualitative implementation challenges including funding competition, maintenance training gaps, and failure/abandonment of some installed units
rationale: Exclude under E03 (Wrong exposure). Although the paper examines community rainwater harvesting systems in Belém, Brazil (c1=yes) using empirical interviews, observations, and Social Network Analysis (c3=yes), it studies multi-stakeholder project delivery, interagency grant-funding brokerage, and Strategic Niche Management in implementing subsidized rainwater infrastructure rather than a rule-type legal, regulatory, or administrative mechanism directly governing household or community service access per the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 clarification (plain=yes, narrow=no).
